themes: Indonesia's accelerating digital-payment adoption and e-commerce penetration are structurally lifting local platform revenue, decoupling IDX tech from US rate-driven volatility.
Government push for domestic cloud and data-sovereignty mandates is creating durable demand for local infrastructure players like IRSX and WGSH, insulating them from global tech capex cycles.
Rising middle-class consumption and rural internet expansion are driving sustained growth in digital media (EMTK) and marketplace (BUKA) monetization, underpinning multi-year earnings compounding.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in Indonesia-listed tech names with local revenue exposure, led by BELI and BUKA, as US weakness rotates capital into IDX digital plays. Favor IRSX and WGSH for structural e-commerce/logistics leverage; trim BHARTIARTL on India concentration. Maintain normal risk, target 12-18% upside over 3 months on IDX tech beta.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech

Climate-tech financing is shifting to IDX-listed vehicles (BREN, CDIA) as green bond issuance and carbon credit monetization create recurring revenue beyond one-off project sales.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in ESSA and CSAP; both are re-rating on firm gas-to-power economics and domestic demand. Rotate out of US-exposed names (BRPT, TPIA) into pure-play ID beneficiaries like CDIA and BREN. Maintain normal exposure; the ID/US divergence widens as local policy tailwinds accelerate project pipelines through Q3.

US infrastructure-linked names face headwinds from a stronger dollar and higher US rates, making domestic-exposed Indonesian players the safer structural bet.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into cement and construction names (SMGR, SMBR) on the back of accelerating government infrastructure disbursements and a recovering property cycle, but trim exposure to US-linked contractors as rate differentials widen. Prioritize domestic-demand plays with pricing power and clear order books; expect continued volatility in small caps, so enter on pullbacks within a 3-6 month horizon.
